records.issue_text: queue.Queue.shutdown() and queue.ShutDown exception only exist in Python 3.13+, so on Python 3.12 or earlier graceful shutdown is impossible and FixedQueuePool.shutdown() raises AttributeError
records.rationale: New code in `src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py` uses Python stdlib APIs that are not present on Python <=3.12: `FixedQueuePool.shutdown()` calls `q.shutdown(immediate=False)` on a `queue.Queue` instance, and `OrderedQueueWorker.run()` catches `except queue.ShutDown:` around `self.work_queue.get()`. In Python 3.12 and earlier, `queue.Queue` has no `shutdown` method and `queue` has no `ShutDown` exception, so this will raise `AttributeError`/fail at runtime, preventing graceful shutdown (and possibly crashing threads).
records.stripped_text: queue.Queue.shutdown() and queue.ShutDown exception only exist in Python 3.13+, so on Python 3.12 or earlier graceful shutdown is impossible and FixedQueuePool.shutdown() raises AttributeError

records.issue_text: Failed messages are marked complete and their offsets committed in the finally block of OrderedQueueWorker.run, silently dropping permanently failed messages with no retry, dead-letter path, or error counter
records.rationale: In `OrderedQueueWorker.run`, `offset_tracker.complete_offset(work_item.partition, work_item.offset)` is executed in the `finally` block unconditionally, even when `result_processor` raises (it is caught by `except Exception:` and only logged). Since the commit loop (`SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy._commit_loop`) computes committable offsets based on `outstanding` being cleared, these failed items can become committable and be committed via `commit_function(committable)` with no retry/dead-letter handling, leading to message loss beyond a log line.

records.issue_text: Offsets completed during the final drain in SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close are never committed on graceful shutdown because the commit thread is joined before queue_pool.shutdown() drains queues, causing duplicate reprocessing on restart
records.rationale: In `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close`, shutdown stops the commit loop before shutting down/finishing worker processing: `self.shutdown_event.set(); self.commit_thread.join(...); self.queue_pool.shutdown()` (new file `queue_consumer.py`). Since the commit loop exits when `shutdown_event` is set, any offsets that become committable while/after workers finish (or partially finish) during `queue_pool.shutdown()` will not be committed. This can lead to duplicate reprocessing after restart due to uncommitted offsets on graceful shutdown.

records.issue_text: terminate() performs a graceful drain instead of a fast terminate and skips joining the commit thread, causing nondeterministic commit state
records.rationale: In `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy`, `terminate()` sets `shutdown_event` and calls `self.queue_pool.shutdown()`, but unlike `close()` it does **not** `join` the `commit_thread` (`close(): self.commit_thread.join(timeout=5.0)`). Also, `queue_pool.shutdown()` is explicitly a *graceful* shutdown (`q.shutdown(immediate=False)` and `worker.join(...)`), so `terminate()` is not a fast/abort-style termination. This combination can leave the commit loop running asynchronously (thread is `daemon=True`) while shutdown proceeds, making commit timing/state nondeterministic.

records.issue_text: FixedQueuePool queues are unbounded (queue.Queue created with no maxsize) and submit never blocks, providing no backpressure, so slower processing than Kafka fetch rate causes unbounded memory growth and eventual OOM
records.rationale: In `FixedQueuePool.__init__`, each queue is created as `queue.Queue()` with no `maxsize` (unbounded). In `FixedQueuePool.submit`, it does `work_queue.put(work_item)`; with an unbounded queue this call will not block, so ingestion can outpace processing and the queue can grow without bound. This also contradicts the `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy` docstring claim of “Natural backpressure when queues fill up.” This is a real risk of unbounded memory growth/OOM under load.

records.rationale: In `TestFixedQueuePool.test_stats_reporting`, after submitting 10 items the test immediately does `stats = self.pool.get_stats(); assert stats["total_items"] > 0`. That means the workers can drain all queues before `get_stats()` runs, making `total_items` legitimately be 0 and the assertion flaky/racy.

If `last_committed` is behind a missing offset that never entered `all_offsets`, and the smallest tracked offset is greater than `last_committed + 1`, the loop starts at `min_offset` and never checks the gap offsets. Example: `last_committed=100`, `all_offsets={102,103}`, `outstanding=∅` => `start=max(101,102)=102`, so it will mark 102/103 committable and return 103, skipping 101 entirely.
